lookback_notes: The assessor's observation/look-back window for Columns 2 and 3 is 7 days (Column 2 = performed while NOT a resident and within the last 7 days; Column 3 = performed while a resident and within the last 7 days). The document states additional, different windows for the other columns: Column 1 assessment period is days 1 through 3 of the SNF PPS Stay starting with A2400B ("Check all nutritional approaches performed during the first 3 days of the SNF PPS Stay", p. K-12), and Column 4 assessment period is the last 3 days of the SNF PPS Stay ending on A2400C ("Check all nutritional approaches performed within the last 3 days of the SNF PPS Stay", p. K-12). Column 2 is left blank if the resident was admitted/entered or reentered more than 7 days ago. The document does not state how the 7 days are counted relative to the ARD for this item.

coding_levels.label: Parenteral/IV feeding
coding_levels.definition: PARENTERAL/IV FEEDING: Introduction of a nutritive substance into the body by means other than the intestinal tract (e.g., subcutaneous, intravenous).

source.quote: PARENTERAL/IV FEEDING Introduction of a nutritive substance into the body by means other than the intestinal tract (e.g., subcutaneous, intravenous).

coding_levels.label: Feeding tube (e.g., nasogastric or abdominal (PEG))
coding_levels.definition: FEEDING TUBE: Presence of any type of tube that can deliver food/ nutritional substances/ fluids directly into the gastrointestinal system. Examples include, but are not limited to, nasogastric tubes, gastrostomy tubes, jejunostomy tubes, percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) tubes.

source.quote: FEEDING TUBE Presence of any type of tube that can deliver food/ nutritional substances/ fluids directly into the gastrointestinal system.

coding_levels.label: Mechanically altered diet
coding_levels.definition: Require change in texture of food or liquids (e.g., pureed food, thickened liquids). MECHANICALLY ALTERED DIET: A diet specifically prepared to alter the texture or consistency of food to facilitate oral intake. Examples include soft solids, puréed foods, ground meat, and thickened liquids.

source.quote: MECHANICALLY ALTERED DIET A diet specifically prepared to alter the texture or consistency of food to facilitate oral intake.

coding_levels.label: Therapeutic diet (e.g., low salt, diabetic, low cholesterol)
coding_levels.definition: THERAPEUTIC DIET: A therapeutic diet is a diet intervention prescribed by a physician or other authorized nonphysician practitioner that provides food or nutrients via oral, enteral, and parenteral routes as part of treatment of disease or clinical condition, to modify, eliminate, decrease, or increase identified micro- and macro-nutrients in the diet (Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, 2020).

source.quote: A therapeutic diet is a diet intervention prescribed by a physician or other authorized nonphysician practitioner that provides food or nutrients via oral, enteral, and parenteral routes as part of treatment of disease or clinical condition

federal_coding_rules.rule: K0520A includes any and all nutrition and hydration received by the nursing home resident during the observation period either at the nursing home, at the hospital as an outpatient or an inpatient, provided they were administered for nutrition or hydration.

source.quote: K0520A includes any and all nutrition and hydration received by the nursing home resident during the observation period either at the nursing home, at the hospital as an outpatient or an inpatient, provided they were administered for nutrition or hydration.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Fluids that may be included in K0520A (when supporting documentation reflects the need for additional fluid intake specifically addressing a nutrition or hydration need): IV fluids or hyperalimentation including total parenteral nutrition (TPN) administered continuously or intermittently; IV fluids running at KVO (Keep Vein Open); IV fluids contained in IV Piggybacks; hypodermoclysis and subcutaneous ports in hydration therapy.

source.quote: IV fluids or hyperalimentation, including total parenteral nutrition (TPN), administered continuously or intermittently

federal_coding_rules.rule: IV fluids can be coded in K0520A if needed to prevent dehydration when the additional fluid intake is specifically needed for nutrition and/or hydration; prevention of dehydration should be clinically indicated and supporting documentation should be provided in the medical record.

source.quote: IV fluids can be coded in K0520A if needed to prevent dehydration if the additional fluid intake is specifically needed for nutrition and/or hydration.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do NOT code in K0520A: IV medications (code in O0110H); IV fluids used to reconstitute and/or dilute medications for IV administration; IV fluids administered as a routine part of an operative or diagnostic procedure or recovery room stay; IV fluids administered solely as flushes; parenteral/IV fluids administered in conjunction with chemotherapy or dialysis.

source.quote: The following items are NOT to be coded in K0520A: — IV Medications—Code these when appropriate in O0110H, IV Medications.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Enteral feeding formulas should not be coded as a mechanically altered diet, and should only be coded as K0520D, Therapeutic Diet when the enteral formula is altered to manage problematic health conditions (e.g., enteral formulas specific to residents with diabetes).

source.quote: Should only be coded as K0520D, Therapeutic Diet when the enteral formula is altered to manage problematic health conditions, e.g. enteral formulas specific to residents with diabetes.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Only feeding tubes that are used to deliver nutritive substances and/or hydration during the assessment period are coded in K0520B.

source.quote: Only feeding tubes that are used to deliver nutritive substances and/or hydration during the assessment period are coded in K0520B.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not capture a trial of a mechanically altered diet (e.g., pureed food, thickened liquids) during the observation period in K0520C.

source.quote: Assessors should not capture a trial of a mechanically altered diet (e.g., pureed food, thickened liquids) during the observation period in K0520C, mechanically altered diet.

federal_coding_rules.rule: A mechanically altered diet should not automatically be considered a therapeutic diet.

source.quote: A mechanically altered diet should not automatically be considered a therapeutic diet.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Therapeutic diets are determined by why the diet is required, not by the content of what is provided or when it is served.

source.quote: Therapeutic diets are not defined by the content of what is provided or when it is served, but why the diet is required.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Nutritional supplements (whether given with, in-between, or instead of meals) are only coded in K0520D, Therapeutic Diet, when they are being administered as part of a therapeutic diet to manage problematic health conditions; a supplement alone does not constitute a therapeutic diet.

source.quote: supplements (whether given with, in-between, or instead of meals) are only coded in K0520D, Therapeutic Diet when they are being administered as part of a therapeutic diet to manage problematic health conditions (e.g. supplement for protein-calorie malnutrition).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Food elimination diets related to food allergies (e.g., peanut allergy) can be coded as a therapeutic diet in K0520D.

source.quote: Food elimination diets related to food allergies (e.g. peanut allergy) can be coded as a therapeutic diet.
